paper_title: Mechanistic Understanding and Mitigation of Language Confusion in   English-Centric Large Language Models
caption: Distribution of Important Neurons Associated with Confusion Points in Llama3-8B. (a) Distribution of the top 300 most important FFN neurons across layers for an individual Chinese prompt “UTF8gbsn请解释拆东墙补西墙的意思。(Please explain `UTF8gbsn拆东墙补西墙.')” from Aya. (b) Aggregated distribution of important neuron scores across all Chinese test samples in Aya.
model_annotation:
Both subplots illustrate how the counts of “Llama3 FFN value neurons” (important neurons) are distributed across transformer layers, with the x-axis labeled “layer” on a linear scale. In (a), the layer axis spans roughly 0 to just past 30 with numeric ticks at regular 5-layer intervals (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30), and the y-axis is labeled “count” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100 with labeled ticks at 20-count intervals (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). In (b), the x-axis is again “layer” on a linear scale extending to about 35 with ticks every 5 layers (0 through 35), and the y-axis is “count” on a linear scale extending to 175 with labeled ticks every 25 counts (25 through 175, with the baseline at 0).

In subplot (a) “Individual Case,” a single blue solid line with circular markers (legend: “Llama3 FFN value neurons”) shows the count per layer for one prompt, with points starting near 0–1 count at the earliest plotted layers (around layers 1–5) and remaining low (generally within single digits) through roughly the mid layers (around layers 10–22), where several points sit between about 2 and 7 counts. In the later layers, the plotted points fluctuate upward and downward around the low-to-mid teens (e.g., points around layers 24–28 include values near ~10–20, with a visible dip back toward ~10 after a local high), followed by a sharp rise at the final few layers: the marker near layer ~29 sits around the mid-20s, the marker near layer ~30 rises to roughly the mid-to-high 70s, and the last marker near layer ~31 is plotted just under 100 (around the mid-90s).

In subplot (b) “Aggregated Neuron Scores,” a single green solid line with circular markers (legend: “Llama3 FFN value neurons”) shows counts per layer aggregated across samples, with the first visible points appearing in the mid layers (around layer ~13) at low values (approximately 3–5 counts). Across layers roughly 13–28, the markers stay clustered in a narrow band in the single digits to around ~10, with small oscillations (several points near ~6–9). Near the end of the x-axis, the series rises steeply: a point around layer ~29 is plotted a bit above 10 (around the mid-teens), the next point near layer ~30 jumps to roughly ~60, and the final point near layer ~31 rises close to the top of the axis at approximately ~170.
